  303: an assessment. Describe the motivation for the research, the results obtained, and the key ideas and methodology in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
LS I +61 303 is a puzzling Be/X-ray binary with variable gamma-ray emission
at up TeV energies. The nature of the compact object and the origin of the
high-energy emission are unclear. One family of models invokes particle
acceleration in shocks from the collision between the B-star wind and a
relativistic pulsar wind, while another centers on a relativistic jet powered
by accretion. Recent high-resolution radio observations showing a putative
"cometary tail" pointing away from the Be star near periastron have been cited
as support for the pulsar-wind model. We wish here to carry out a quantitative
assessment of these competing models for this extraordinary source. We apply a
3D SPH code for dynamical simulations of both the pulsar-wind-interaction and
accretion-jet models. The former yields a description of the shape of the
wind-wind interaction surface. The latter provides an estimation of the
accretion rate. The results allow critical evaluation of how the two distinct
models confront the data in various wavebands under a range of conditions. When
one accounts for the 3D dynamical wind interaction under realistic constraints
for the relative strength of the B-star and pulsar winds, the resulting form of
the interaction front does not match the putative "cometary tail" claimed from
radio observations. On the other hand, dynamical simulations of the
accretion-jet model indicate that the orbital phase variation of accretion
power includes a secondary broad peak well away from periastron, thus providing
a plausible way to explain the observed TeV gamma ray emission toward apastron.
We conclude that the colliding-wind model is not clearly established for LS I
+61 303, while the accretion-jet model can reproduce many key characteristics
of the observed TeV gamma-ray emission.
machine_text:
In this paper, we present our assessment of the Accretion vs Colliding Wind (AVCW) models for the gamma-ray binary LS I +61 303, which has been a topic of controversy among the astrophysical community. The motivation behind our research was the need to clarify the origin of the gamma-ray emission in this binary. Our methodology involved the use of non-LTE radiative transfer simulation to construct synthetic spectra, which were then compared with the observed data. We also made use of Chandra and HST observations to study the X-ray and optical emission, respectively.

Our results suggest that the colliding wind scenario is favored over the accretion scenario since it better reproduces the observed gamma-ray spectrum of LS I +61 303. Furthermore, the colliding wind model is able to explain the observed behavior of the binary on larger timescales. This result is consistent with previous studies that have suggested that colliding wind interactions between high mass stars can produce non-thermal gamma-ray emission.

In conclusion, our study provides new insights into the nature of gamma-ray emission in LS I +61 303, and adds to the growing body of evidence that suggests colliding wind models are a viable mechanism for producing non-thermal radiation in high-mass binary systems.

Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Detailed study of the GRB 030329 radio afterglow deep into the
  non-relativistic phase. Describe  problem work attempts to solve, the motivation for the research, and the results obtained in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We explore the physics behind one of the brightest radio afterglows ever, GRB
030329, at late times when the jet is non-relativistic. We determine the
physical parameters of the blast wave and its surroundings, in particular the
index of the electron energy distribution, the energy of the blast wave, and
the density (structure) of the circumburst medium. We then compare our results
with those from image size measurements. We observed the GRB 030329 radio
afterglow with the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope and the Giant Metrewave
Radio Telescope at frequencies from 325 MHz to 8.4 GHz, spanning a time range
of 268-1128 days after the burst. We modeled all the available radio data and
derived the physical parameters. The index of the electron energy distribution
is p=2.1, the circumburst medium is homogeneous, and the transition to the
non-relativistic phase happens at t_NR ~ 80 days. The energy of the blast wave
and density of the surrounding medium are comparable to previous findings. Our
findings indicate that the blast wave is roughly spherical at t_NR, and they
agree with the implications from the VLBI studies of image size evolution. It
is not clear from the presented dataset whether we have seen emission from the
counter jet or not. We predict that the Low Frequency Array will be able to
observe the afterglow of GRB 030329 and many other radio afterglows,
constraining the physics of the blast wave during its non-relativistic phase
even further.

In this work, we present a detailed study of the radio afterglow from GRB 030329, a gamma-ray burst event occurring in 2003. The main aim of our research is to investigate the non-relativistic phase of the afterglow emission, which occurs after the initial relativistic blast wave. Previous studies have mainly focused on the relativistic phase, neglecting the non-relativistic phase, which is crucial in understanding the physics of these events.

Our motivation for this research is to shed light on the mechanism of the afterglow emission, which is still not fully understood. By studying the non-relativistic phase, we hope to contribute to the understanding of the interaction between the ejecta and the circumburst medium. We performed radio observations using the Very Large Array (VLA) at multiple frequencies, which enabled us to study the temporal and spectral evolution of the afterglow emission.

Our results reveal important insights into the physics of the afterglow emission, such as evidence of inverse Compton scattering, which indicates the presence of relativistic electrons. Furthermore, we observe the evolution of the radio spectral index, which is consistent with the standard afterglow model. Our findings suggest that the non-relativistic phase plays a crucial role in shaping the afterglow emission, and thereby aids in understanding the physical processes behind gamma-ray bursts.

Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Thermodynamics and the virial expansion for trapped fluids in arbitrary
  external potentials. Describe the key ideas and methodology, the results obtained, and the motivation for the research in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We present the full thermodynamics of a fluid confined by an arbitrary
external potential based on the virial expansion of the grand potential. The
fluid may be classical or quantum and it is assumed that interatomic
interactions are pairwise additive. We indicate how the appropriate
"generalized" volume and pressure variables, that replace the usual volume and
hydrostatic pressure, emerge for a given confining potential in the
thermodynamic limit. A discussion of the physical meaning and of the
measurement of these variables is presented. We emphasize that this treatment
yields the correct equation of state of the fluid and we give its virial
expansion. We propose an experiment to measure the heat capacity, so that with
this quantity and the equation of state, the complete thermodynamics of the
system may be extracted. As a corollary, we find that the so-called {\it local
density approximation} for these systems follows in the thermodynamic limit,
although we also point out that it cannot be used indiscriminately for all
local variables. Along the text we discuss the relevance of these findings in
the description of the currently confined ultracold gases.
machine_text:
In this work, we explore the thermodynamics and virial expansion for trapped fluids in arbitrary external potentials. Our aim is to understand the behavior of fluids confined in complex spatial geometries, such as those encountered in microfluidic devices and biological systems. To achieve this, we employ a combination of theoretical and computational methods rooted in statistical mechanics and thermodynamics.

Using a virial expansion, we derive expressions for the equation of state and thermodynamic properties of the confined fluid as a function of temperature and confinement geometry. We show that these properties depend crucially on the spatial distribution of the external potential and the degree of confinement.

Our results demonstrate that the thermodynamic behavior of confined fluids can be significantly altered in the presence of complex spatial geometries. We find that the virial coefficients exhibit non-monotonic dependence on temperature, leading to the emergence of non-trivial thermodynamic states, such as multiple phase transitions and criticality.

The motivation for this research is to provide a theoretical foundation for understanding the thermodynamic properties of fluids in complex environments, with implications for the design and optimization of microfluidic devices and biological systems. Our findings have implications for a broad range of scientific fields, including soft matter physics, biophysics, and chemical engineering.

Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Solidity of viscous liquids. V. Long-wavelength dominance of the
  dynamics. Describe the key ideas and methodology, the results obtained, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
This paper is the fifth in a series exploring the physical consequences of
the solidity of glass-forming liquids. Paper IV proposed a model where the
density field is described by a time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equation of the
nonconserved type with rates in $k$ space of the form $\Gamma_0+Dk^2$. The
model assumes that $D\gg\Gamma_0a^2$ where $a$ is the average intermolecular
distance; this inequality expresses a long-wavelength dominance of the dynamics
which implies that the Hamiltonian (free energy) to a good approximation may be
taken to be ultralocal. In the present paper we argue that this is the simplest
model consistent with the following three experimental facts: 1) Viscous
liquids approaching the glass transition do not develop long-range order; 2)
The glass has lower compressibility than the liquid; 3) The alpha process
involves several decades of relaxation times shorter than the mean relaxation
time. The paper proceeds to list six further experimental facts characterizing
equilibrium viscous liquid dynamics and shows that these are readily understood
in terms of the model; some are direct consequences, others are quite natural
when viewed in light of the model.

Our methodology involves using a theoretical framework that combines stochastic calculus and hydrodynamics. We aim to solve the problem of understanding the relationship between viscosity and solidification in these materials, which has important practical implications for materials science and industry. Our results suggest that the dynamics of viscous liquids are dominated by long-wavelength behavior, and that this is related to the presence of solid-like structures within the liquid. We observe a crossover from liquid-like to solid-like behavior as the wavelength of the perturbations is increased. Our work provides a deeper understanding of the behavior of viscous liquids, and could help to inform the design of new materials with improved properties. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of understanding the interplay between viscosity and solidification in these systems, and the potential for further research in this area.

prompt:
Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Transients from initial conditions based on Lagrangian perturbation
  theory in N-body simulations. Describe the motivation for the research, the key ideas and methodology, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We explore the initial conditions for cosmological N-body simulations
suitable for calculating the skewness and kurtosis of the density field. In
general, the initial conditions based on the perturbation theory (PT) provide
incorrect second-order and higher-order growth. These errors implied by the use
of the perturbation theory to set up the initial conditions in N-body
simulations are called transients. Unless these transients are completely
suppressed compared with the dominant growing mode, we can not reproduce the
correct evolution of cumulants with orders higher than two, even though there
is no problem with the numerical scheme. We investigate the impact of
transients on the observable statistical quantities by performing $N$-body
simulations with initial conditions based on Lagrangian perturbation theory
(LPT). We show that the effects of transients on the kurtosis from the initial
conditions, based on second-order Lagrangian perturbation theory (2LPT) have
almost disappeared by $z\sim5$, as long as the initial conditions are set at $z
> 30$. This means that for practical purposes, the initial conditions based on
2LPT are accurate enough for numerical calculations of skewness and kurtosis.
machine_text: In this paper, we present a study focused on the understanding of transients from initial conditions in N-body simulations using Lagrangian perturbation theory. N-body simulations are one of the primary tools in cosmology to explore the evolution of large-scale structures in the Universe. However, the precise reproduction of observed galaxy clustering statistics remains a challenge. A major source of systematic errors comes from the initial conditions, which are typically generated using linear perturbation theory assumptions. We propose a novel approach that employs Lagrangian perturbation theory to compute the initial conditions for the simulations, thereby accounting for non-linear effects that can have a significant impact on the final clustering statistics. Our proposal is based on the idea that high-order corrections can be systematically included and give rise to non-Gaussianities in the initial conditions. The methodology is tested on a set of numerical experiments, where we demonstrate that our approach leads to improved results in the clustering statistics even on large scales. Our work aims to contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable simulation tools that can be used to test cosmological models and explore the fundamental properties of the Universe.

  early dark energy. Describe the results obtained, the key ideas and methodology, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
In the standard Lambda CDM cosmological model with a Gaussian primordial
density fluctuation field, the relatively low value of the mass variance
parameter (sigma_8=0.74{+0.05}{-0.06}, obtained from the WMAP 3-year data)
results in a reduced likelihood that the measured level of CMB anisotropy on
the scales of clusters is due to the Sunyaev-Zeldovich (S-Z) effect. To assess
the feasibility of producing higher levels of S-Z power, we explore two
alternative models which predict higher cluster abundance. In the first model
the primordial density field has a chi^2_1 distribution, whereas in the second
an early dark energy component gives rise to the desired higher cluster
abundance. We carry out the necessary detailed calculations of the levels of
S-Z power spectra, cluster number counts, and angular 2-point correlation
function of clusters, and compare (in a self-consistent way) their predicted
redshift distributions. Our results provide a sufficient basis upon which the
viability of the three models may be tested by future high quality
measurements.

In this work, we investigate the effects of non-Gaussianity and early dark energy on the cluster abundances and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (S-Z) power spectra. Non-Gaussianity is a deviation from the Gaussian distribution assumption that is made in many cosmological models. Early dark energy is a hypothetical form of energy that can affect the evolution of the universe in the very early stages of its history. We use numerical simulations to study the impact of these two factors on the cluster abundances and S-Z power spectra.

Our results show that non-Gaussianity can significantly alter the cluster abundance and S-Z power spectrum. In particular, the amplitude of the S-Z power spectrum is increased in non-Gaussian scenarios. Our results also demonstrate that early dark energy can affect the cluster abundance and S-Z power spectrum, but the effect is less significant than that of non-Gaussianity.

The key idea behind this work is to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the impact of non-Gaussianity and early dark energy on the cluster abundances and S-Z power spectra. The methodology involves running numerical simulations and analyzing the resulting data.

prompt: Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: A Study in Depth of f0(1370). Describe the results obtained, the key ideas and methodology, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
Claims have been made that f0(1370) does not exist. The five primary sets of
data requiring its existence are refitted. Major dispersive effects due to the
opening of the 4pi threshold are included for the first time; the sigma -> 4pi
amplitude plays a strong role. Crystal Barrel data on pbar-p -> 3pizero at rest
require f0(1370) signals of at least 32 and 33 standard deviations in 1S0 and
3P1 annihilation respectively. Furthermore, they agree within 5 MeV for mass
and width. Data on pbar-p -> eta-eta-pizero agree and require at least a 19
standard deviation contribution. This alone is sufficient to demonstrate the
existence of f0(1370). BES II data for J/Psi -> phi-pi-pi contain a visible
f0(1370) signal > 8 standard devations. In all cases, a resonant phase
variation is required. The possibility of a second pole in the sigma amplitude
due to the opening of the 4pi channel is excluded. Cern-Munich data for pi-pi
elastic scattering are fitted well with the inclusion of some mixing between
sigma, f0(1370) and f0(1500). The pi-pi widths for f2(1565), rho3(1690),
rho3(1990) and f4(2040) are determined.

In this study, we explored the characteristics and behavior of the f0(1370) resonance using data from the CLAS detector at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility. We aimed to understand the underlying physics and structure of this resonance, which has been a topic of interest and debate in the field of meson spectroscopy for several decades. 

Our analysis revealed strong evidence of two overlapping states, with masses of approximately 1350 MeV and 1420 MeV, respectively. We also observed significant decay branching ratios and angular distributions, which provided insight into the possible nature of the f0(1370). Through our examination of the available data, we proposed a model that involved the presence of both a scalar and a mixed-symmetry tensor component in the resonance. 

To obtain these results, we used a combination of Monte Carlo simulations, fits to invariant mass distributions, and partial wave analysis techniques. Our methodology involved a careful examination of the systematic uncertainties and limitations of our measurements, in order to ensure the validity of our conclusions. 

Overall, our study provides a significant contribution to the understanding of the f0(1370) resonance and its properties. This work has the potential to inform future investigations and theoretical developments in the field of meson spectroscopy.

prompt: Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Low-temperature electron dephasing time in AuPd revisited. Describe  problem work attempts to solve, the results obtained, and the motivation for the research in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
Ever since the first discoveries of the quantum-interference transport in
mesoscopic systems, the electron dephasing times, $\tau_\phi$, in the
concentrated AuPd alloys have been extensively measured. The samples were made
from different sources with different compositions, prepared by different
deposition methods, and various geometries (1D narrow wires, 2D thin films, and
3D thickfilms) were studied. Surprisingly, the low-temperature behavior of
$\tau_\phi$ inferred by different groups over two decades reveals a systematic
correlation with the level of disorder of the sample. At low temperatures,
where $\tau_\phi$ is (nearly) independent of temperature, a scaling
$\tau_\phi^{\rm max} \propto D^{-\alpha}$ is found, where $tau_\phi^{\rm max}$
is the maximum value of $\tau_\phi$ measured in the experiment, $D$ is the
electron diffusion constant, and the exponent $\alpha$ is close to or slightly
larger than 1. We address this nontrivial scaling behavior and suggest that the
most possible origin for this unusual dephasing is due to dynamical structure
defects, while other theoretical explanations may not be totally ruled out.
machine_text: In this work, we revisit the electron dephasing time in AuPd alloys at low temperatures. Understanding dephasing times is critical for characterizing the coherence of electronic states and for developing new electronic devices. Despite extensive studies on the dephasing of electrons in metals, there is no consensus on the nature of the dephasing mechanisms at low temperatures. In order to provide further insight into the behavior of electrons in AuPd alloys, we perform magnetoconductance measurements on an epitaxial AuPd film in a dilution refrigerator. The electron dephasing time is extracted from the temperature-dependence of the magnetoconductance in the weak localization regime. We find that the size of the AuPd grain structure significantly influences the electron dephasing time at low temperatures. Our results indicate that electron-electron scattering dominates the dephasing mechanism at low temperatures rather than electron-phonon scattering. The nature of the dephasing mechanism is directly related to the electronic structure and the Fermi energy of the alloy. Our findings may contribute to the development of new electronic devices that harness the unique properties of AuPd alloys.

Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Spectroscopy and multiband photometry of the afterglow of intermediate
  duration gamma-ray burst 040924 and its host galaxy. Describe the motivation for the research, the key ideas and methodology, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We present optical photometry and spectroscopy of the afterglow and host
galaxy of gamma-ray burst 040924. This GRB had a rather short duration of T90
~2.4s, and a well sampled optical afterglow light curve. We aim to use this
dataset to find further evidence that this burst is consistent with a massive
star core-collapse progenitor. We combine the afterglow data reported here with
data taken from the literature and compare the host properties with survey
data. We find that the global behaviour of the optical afterglow is well fit by
a broken power-law, with a break at ~0.03 days. We determine the redshift z =
0.858 +/- 0.001 from the detected emission lines in our spectrum. Using the
spectrum and photometry we derive global properties of the host, showing it to
have similar properties to long GRB hosts. We detect the [Ne III] emission line
in the spectrum, and compare the fluxes of this line of a sample of 15 long GRB
host galaxies with survey data, showing the long GRB hosts to be comparable to
local metal-poor emission line galaxies in their [Ne III] emission. We fit the
supernova bump accompanying this burst, and find that it is similar to other
long GRB supernova bumps, but fainter. All properties of GRB 040924 are
consistent with an origin in the core-collapse of a massive star: the
supernova, the spectrum and SED of the host and the afterglow.

In this work, we present the results of spectroscopy and multiband photometry of the afterglow of intermediate duration gamma-ray burst 040924 and its host galaxy. Our main motivation for conducting this research was to understand the physical properties of these transient events and their host galaxies. Gamma-ray bursts are one of the most energetic events that occur in the universe. They are also important probes of the early universe as they are detectable out to high redshifts. Our aim was to investigate the nature of these events in the context of their host galaxies.

We obtained spectroscopic observations of the host galaxy using the Keck telescope and multiband photometry using several telescopes including Swift, TNG and RATIR. Our key idea was to use the afterglow observations to derive the physical properties of the afterglow shock. This allowed us to study the properties of the host galaxy and compare them with those of other host galaxies.

Our analysis of the data revealed several interesting results. We found that the host galaxy of 040924 is a low-metallicity star-forming galaxy. Moreover, the origin of the gamma-ray burst is likely to be related to the core-collapse of a massive star. Our work provides important insights into the physical properties of intermediate duration gamma-ray bursts and their host galaxies.

  and multiple systems. Describe  problem work attempts to solve, the key ideas and methodology, and the motivation for the research in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.

The results of the Koenigstuhl survey in the Southern Hemisphere are
presented. I have searched for common-proper motion companions to 173 field
very low-mass stars and brown dwarfs with spectral types > M5.0V and magnitudes
J <= 14.5 mag. I have measured for the first time the common-proper motion of
two new wide systems containing very low-mass components, Koenigstuhl 2 AB and
3 A-BC. Together with Koenigstuhl 1 AB and 2M0126-50AB, they are among the
widest systems in their respective classes (r = 450-11900 AU). Koenigstuhl 3
A-BC contains a well-known F8V star and a M8.0+L3.0V tight binary. I have
determined the minimum frequency of field wide multiples (r > 100 AU) with
late-type components at 5.0+/-1.8 % and the frequency of field wide late-type
binaries with mass ratios q > 0.5 at 1.2+/-0.9 %. These values represent a key
diagnostic of evolution history and low-mass star and brown-dwarf formation
scenarios. Additionally, the proper motions of 76 field very low-mass dwarfs
are measured here for the first time.

prompt: Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: The Anisotropic Distribution of Satellite Galaxies. Describe  problem work attempts to solve, the motivation for the research, and the results obtained in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We identify satellites of isolated galaxies in SDSS and examine their angular
distribution. Using mock catalogues generated from cosmological N-body
simulations, we demonstrate that the selection criteria used to select isolated
galaxies and their satellites must be very strict in order to correctly
identify systems in which the primary galaxy dominates its environment. The
criteria used in many previous studies instead select predominantly group
members. We refine a set of selection criteria for which the group
contamination is estimated to be less than 7% and present a catalogue of the
resulting sample. The angular distribution of satellites about their host is
biased towards the major axes for spheroidal galaxies and probably also for red
disc galaxies, but is isotropic for blue disc galaxies, i.e. it is the colour
of the host that determines the distribution of its satellites rather than its
morphology. The similar anisotropy measured in this study as in studies that
were dominated by groups implies that group-specific processes are not
responsible for the angular distribution. Satellites that are most likely to
have been recently accreted show a tendancy to lie along the same axis as the
surrounding large scale structure. The orientations of isolated early and
intermediate-type galaxies also align with the surrounding large scale
structures. We discuss the origin of the anisotropic satellite distribution and
consider the implications of our results, critically assessing the respective
roles played by the orientation of the visible galaxy within its dark matter
halo; anisotropic accretion of satellites from the larger scale environment;
and the biased nature of satellites as tracers of the underlying dark matter
subhalo population. (Abridged)
machine_text:
In this work, we investigate the anisotropic distribution of satellite galaxies around their isolated central galaxies. Our motivation for this research stems from the fact that the orientation of these satellite galaxies can provide insights into the formation and evolution of their host galaxies, which in turn can lead to a better understanding of the larger scale structures of the universe. Specifically, we test the hypothesis that the satellites' orientations are preferentially aligned with the central galaxy's major axis. 

To investigate this hypothesis, we construct a sample of central galaxies taken from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and select their surrounding satellites. We then measure the alignment between the major axis of each central galaxy and the axes of its surrounding satellites. We find that, on average, satellite galaxies are preferentially oriented along a plane perpendicular to the direction of the central galaxy’s major axis, which suggests that the central galaxy's effect on its surrounding environment is stronger than previously thought. Moreover, we find that this anisotropic distribution is more prominent for high-mass central galaxies than for low-mass ones. These results shed light on the intricate interplay between central galaxies and their satellite galaxies, emphasizing the importance of their mutual interactions in shaping the universe's large-scale structures.

Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: New 60-cm Radio Survey Telescope with the Sideband-Separating SIS
  Receiver for the 200 GHz Band. Describe the motivation for the research,  problem work attempts to solve, and the results obtained in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
We have upgraded the 60-cm radio survey telescope located in Nobeyama, Japan.
We developed a new waveguide-type sideband-separating SIS mixer for the
telescope, which enables the simultaneous detection of distinct molecular
emission lines both in the upper and lower sidebands. Over the RF frequency
range of 205-240 GHz, the single-sideband receiver noise temperatures of the
new mixer are 40-100 K for the 4.0-8.0 GHz IF frequency band. The image
rejection ratios are greater than 10 dB over the same range. For the dual IF
signals obtained by the receiver, we have developed two sets of acousto-optical
spectrometers and a telescope control system. Using the new telescope system,
we successfully detected the 12CO (J=2-1) and 13CO (J=2-1) emission lines
simultaneously toward Orion KL in 2005 March. Using the waveguide-type
sideband-separating SIS mixer for the 200 GHz band, we have initiated the first
simultaneous 12CO (J=2-1) and 13CO (J=2-1) survey of the galactic plane as well
as large-scale mapping observations of nearby molecular clouds.

The installation of a sensitive and high-resolution telescope, specifically optimized for this band, is a significant contribution to the current state of observational radio astronomy.

The previous instruments had either limited sensitivity or poor spectral resolution, thereby making it hard to study faint and small-scale features. The 60-cm Radio Survey Telescope with Sideband-Separating SIS receiver for the 200 GHz Band is now open for regular observing programs and will undoubtedly yield a wealth of science.

prompt: Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Water's Hydrogen Bond Strength. Describe the results obtained, the motivation for the research, and  problem work attempts to solve in a formal academic and scientific writing voice. Use the first plural person form. Use active voice.
human_text:
Water is necessary both for the evolution of life and its continuance. It
possesses particular properties that cannot be found in other materials and
that are required for life-giving processes. These properties are brought about
by the hydrogen bonded environment particularly evident in liquid water. Each
liquid water molecule is involved in about four hydrogen bonds with strengths

prediction of the upcoming large event.

weak interchain-coupling regime. The dynamical spin correlations from this
approach agree quantitatively with inelastic neutron measurements on the

antiferromagnets can be attributed to two types of excitations: descendents of
one-dimensional spinons of individual chains, and coherently propagating
"triplon" bound states of spinon pairs. We argue that triplons are generic
features of spatially anisotropic frustrated antiferromagnets, and arise
because the bound spinon pair lowers its kinetic energy by propagating between
chains.

prompt: Generate a 150-220-word abstract for work with title: Generation interval contraction and epidemic data analysis. person and the infection time of his or her infector. Probability density
functions for generation intervals have been an important input for epidemic
models and epidemic data analysis. In this paper, we specify a general
stochastic SIR epidemic model and prove that the mean generation interval
decreases when susceptible persons are at risk of infectious contact from
multiple sources. The intuition behind this is that when a susceptible person
has multiple potential infectors, there is a ``race'' to infect him or her in
which only the first infectious contact leads to infection. In an epidemic, the
mean generation interval contracts as the prevalence of infection increases. We
call this global competition among potential infectors. When there is rapid
transmission within clusters of contacts, generation interval contraction can
be caused by a high local prevalence of infection even when the global
prevalence is low. We call this local competition among potential infectors.
Using simulations, we illustrate both types of competition.
  Finally, we show that hazards of infectious contact can be used instead of
generation intervals to estimate the time course of the effective reproductive
number in an epidemic. This approach leads naturally to partial likelihoods for
epidemic data that are very similar to those that arise in survival analysis,
opening a promising avenue of methodological research in infectious disease
epidemiology.

Let G be a graph with maximum degree \Delta whose vertex set is partitioned
into parts V(G) = V_1 \cup ... \cup V_r. A transversal is a subset of V(G)
containing exactly one vertex from each part V_i. If it is also an independent
set, then we call it an independent transversal. The local degree of G is the
maximum number of neighbors of a vertex v in a part V_i, taken over all choices
of V_i and v \not \in V_i. We prove that for every fixed \epsilon > 0, if all
part sizes |V_i| >= (1+\epsilon)\Delta and the local degree of G is o(\Delta),
then G has an independent transversal for sufficiently large \Delta. This
extends several previous results and settles (in a stronger form) a conjecture
of Aharoni and Holzman. We then generalize this result to transversals that
induce no cliques of size s. (Note that independent transversals correspond to
s=2.) In that context, we prove that parts of size |V_i| >=
(1+\epsilon)[\Delta/(s-1)] and local degree o(\Delta) guarantee the existence
of such a transversal, and we provide a construction that shows this is
asymptotically tight.

charge and three-current operators. If these nuclear operators are approximated

performed in a basis of Slater determinants formed from harmonic oscillator
orbitals, a choice that allows translational invariance to be preserved.

can be evaluated analytically and expressed in terms of finite polynomials in
q^2, where q is the magnitude of the three-momentum transfer. While results for
such matrix elements are available in tabular form, with certain restriction on
quantum numbers, the task of determining the analytic form of a response
function can still be quite tedious, requiring the folding of the tabulated
matrix elements with the nuclear density matrix, and subsequent algebra to
evaluate products of operators. Here we provide a Mathematica script for
generating these matrix elements, which will allow users to carry out all such
calculations by symbolic manipulation. This will eliminate the errors that may
accompany hand calculations and speed the calculation of electroweak nuclear
cross sections and rates. We illustrate the use of the new script by
calculating the cross sections for charged- and neutral-current neutrino
scattering in ^{12}C.

further interesting family of non-toric Gizatullin surfaces, called the

classes of $\bf C^*$-actions and $\bf A^1$-fibrations.

for which a $\bf C^*$-action is essentially unique and for which there are at
most two conjugacy classes of $\bf A^1$-fibrations over $\bf A^1$.
